cases.sentence: Говорят, у Тургенева от подагры сделалась ___.
cases.explain: «грудная жаба» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: SEREBRAKOFF. They say that Turgenieff got angina of the heart from gout. I am afraid I am getting angina too. Oh, damn this horrible, accursed old age! Ever since I have been old I have been hateful to myself, and I am sure, hateful to you all as well.

cases.sentence: Странное дело, заговорит Иван Петрович или эта ___, Марья Васильевна, — и ничего, все слушают, но скажи я хоть одно слово, как все начинают чувствовать себя несчастными.
cases.explain: «старая идиотка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: SEREBRAKOFF. It is funny that everybody listens to Ivan and his old idiot of a mother, but the moment I open my lips you all begin to feel ill-treated. You can't even stand the sound of my voice. Even if I am hateful, even if I am a selfish tyrant, haven't I the right to be one at my age? Haven't I deserved it? Haven't I, I ask you, the right to be respected, now that I am old?

cases.sentence: Всю жизнь работать для науки, привыкнуть к своему кабинету, к аудитории, к ___ — и вдруг, ни с того ни с сего, очутиться в этом склепе, каждый день видеть тут глупых людей, слушать ничтожные разговоры…
cases.explain: «почтенным товарищам» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: SEREBRAKOFF. I have spent my life working in the interests of learning. I am used to my library and the lecture hall and to the esteem and admiration of my colleagues. Now I suddenly find myself plunged in this wilderness, condemned to see the same stupid people from morning till night and listen to their futile conversation. I want to live; I long for success and fame and the stir of the world, and here I am in exile! Oh, it is dreadful to spend every moment grieving for the lost past, to see the success of others and sit here with nothing to do but to fear death. I cannot stand it! It is more than I can bear. And you will not even forgive me for being old!

cases.sentence: Не выписывать же сюда для твоей подагры целый ___.
cases.explain: «медицинский факультет» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: SONIA. We can't send for the whole medical faculty, can we, to treat your gout?

cases.sentence: Во имя нашей ___, не протестуй.
cases.explain: «прежней дружбы» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: SEREBRAKOFF. Then let them go to bed, but you go away too! Thank you. I implore you to go. For the sake of our former friendship do not protest against going. We will talk some other time---

cases.sentence: У меня у ___ гудут, так и гудут.
cases.explain: «самой ноги» — after the preposition «у», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: MARINA. [Goes up to SEREBRAKOFF and speaks tenderly] What's the matter, master? Does it hurt? My own legs are aching too, oh, so badly. [Arranges his shawl about his legs] You have had this illness such a long time. Sonia's dead mother used to stay awake with you too, and wear herself out for you. She loved you dearly. [A pause] Old people want to be pitied as much as young ones, but nobody cares about them somehow. [She kisses SEREBRAKOFF'S shoulder] Come, master, let me give you some linden-tea and warm your poor feet for you. I shall pray to God for you.

cases.sentence: Я берусь за самые ___ и делаю их прекрасно; я рисую самые широкие планы будущего; в это время я уже не кажусь себе чудаком и верю, что приношу человечеству громадную пользу… громадную!
cases.explain: «трудные операции» — after the preposition «за», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: ASTROFF. What do you mean? Yes, I must confess I am getting vulgar, but then, you see, I am drunk. I usually only drink like this once a month. At such times my audacity and temerity know no bounds. I feel capable of anything. I attempt the most difficult operations and do them magnificently. The most brilliant plans for the future take shape in my head. I am no longer a poor fool of a doctor, but mankind's greatest benefactor. I evolve my own system of philosophy and all of you seem to crawl at my feet like so many insects or microbes. [To TELEGIN] Play, Waffles!

cases.sentence: Подружились ___.
cases.explain: «ясные соколы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: SONIA. Uncle Vanya, you and the doctor have been drinking! The good fellows have been getting together! It is all very well for him, he has always done it, but why do you follow his example? It looks dreadfully at your age.

cases.sentence: (Жадно целует ее руки и лицо.) Сестра моя… ___ моя… где она теперь?
cases.explain: «милая сестра» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: VOITSKI. Tears? Nonsense, there are no tears in my eyes. You looked at me then just as your dead mother used to, my darling--[He eagerly kisses her face and hands] My sister, my dearest sister, where are you now? Ah, if you only knew, if you only knew!

cases.sentence: Он в жизни, говорят, имел ___ у женщин, и его дамы избаловали.
cases.explain: «большой успех» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: SONIA. I love to eat at night. I am sure we shall find something in here. They say that he has made a great many conquests in his life, and that the women have spoiled him. Here is some cheese for you. [They stand eating by the sideboard.]

cases.sentence: Зачем же вы хотите походить на ___, которые пьют и играют в карты?
cases.explain: «обыкновенных людей» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: SONIA. It is so unworthy of you. You are well-bred, your voice is sweet, you are even--more than any one I know--handsome. Why do you want to resemble the common people that drink and play cards? Oh, don't, I beg you! You always say that people do not create anything, but only destroy what heaven has given them. Why, oh, why, do you destroy yourself? Oh, don't, I implore you not to! I entreat you!

cases.sentence: Не говорим мы друг с другом по ___ и бог знает из-за чего…
cases.explain: «целым неделям» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: HELENA. No, he is sitting up in the drawing-room. Heaven knows what reason you and I had for not speaking to each other for weeks. [Sees the open sideboard] Who left the sideboard open?

cases.sentence: Скажи откровенно, — ты хотела бы, чтобы у тебя был ___?
cases.explain: «молодой муж» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: SONIA. I knew it. One more question: do you wish your husband were young?

cases.sentence: Смелость, ___, широкий размах…
cases.explain: «свободная голова» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: HELENA. It is not a question of medicine and woods, my dear, he is a man of genius. Do you know what that means? It means he is brave, profound, and of clear insight. He plants a tree and his mind travels a thousand years into the future, and he sees visions of the happiness of the human race. People like him are rare and should be loved. What if he does drink and act roughly at times? A man of genius cannot be a saint in Russia. There he lives, cut off from the world by cold and storm and endless roads of bottomless mud, surrounded by a rough people who are crushed by poverty and disease, his life one continuous struggle, with never a day's respite; how can a man live like that for forty years and keep himself sober and unspotted? [Kissing SONIA] I wish you happiness with all my heart; you deserve it. [She gets up] As for me, I am a worthless, futile woman. I have always been futile; in music, in love, in my husband's house--in a word, in everything. When you come to think of it, Sonia, I am really very, very unhappy. [Walks excitedly up and down] Happiness can never exist for me in this world. Never. Why do you laugh?
